brain.query.search.label: Search your knowledge base
brain.query.search.placeholder: What do you want to find?
brain.query.group.question: The question
brain.query.projection.tooltip: A JSON object choosing which fields each result carries, e.g. { "description": 1 }. It can exclude as well as include. Leave empty for whole records — a projection that omits the field you are reading gives a result that looks complete and is missing the answer.
brain.query.projectionMustBeObject: The fields-returned box must be a JSON object, not an array or a value.
brain.query.projectionInvalidJson: The fields-returned box is not valid JSON.
brain.query.direction.tooltip: Which way to walk from a match. Outbound from a person reaches what they own; inbound reaches who named them. A walk that ignores the difference answers another question and looks the same.
brain.query.edgeLabels.tooltip: Restrict the walk to edges carrying these labels. Comma-separated; empty follows every label.
brain.query.maxChars.tooltip: The same ceiling as bytes, counted in characters. Not the same number outside plain ASCII — the two differ by about a quarter in German or Polish. Empty uses the default.
brain.query.maxTokens.tooltip: The same ceiling in tokens, which is the unit an agent budget is written in. Set more than one unit and the smallest one wins.
brain.query.charsPerToken.tooltip: How the token ceiling is converted. Only used when a token ceiling is set.
brain.query.skip.tooltip: Skip this many ranked matches. When an answer is shortened it reports where to continue from — put that number here. It is absolute, not a page number.
brain.query.remainderDump.tooltip: Write the matches that were cut off to a file in this space, downloadable for one day.
brain.query.remainderDump.writes: This WRITES a JSON file into this space. It is the only setting on this form that changes anything.
brain.query.request.label: The request this would send
brain.query.request.empty: Type a question and the request appears here.
brain.query.request.invalid: No request yet — one of the JSON boxes above is not a valid object.
brain.query.request.hint: This is exactly what the Search button sends. Paste it into a recall call over MCP or REST and you get the same answer.
brain.query.topK.tooltip: Maximum number of results to return
brain.query.minScore.tooltip: Minimum similarity score (0–1). Higher = more relevant.
brain.query.maxPerType.tooltip: Cap how many hits each knowledge type may contribute, so one noisy type cannot fill the whole result set. Empty or 0 means no cap.
brain.query.traverse.tooltip: Expand each match along knowledge-graph edges, 0–5 hops. Connected entities are returned alongside the matches, marked with how many hops away they are and which edges connect them. 0 (default) does no expansion. Deep values on a dense graph are slow — narrow the seeds with a filter or tags first.
brain.query.recallMaxTimeMs.tooltip: Deadline for this recall, in milliseconds. It can only lower the instance budget, never raise it. On expiry you get a PARTIAL answer rather than an error: whichever knowledge types finished are returned, and the response says it degraded. Leave empty for the instance default.
brain.query.recallMaxBytes.tooltip: Ceiling on the size of the answer, in bytes. The results you get are the top of the ranking and every record is complete — never half a passage, never a record missing part of its graph. Past the ceiling the answer is shortened and the page says so. Leave empty for the instance default (100000). The floor is 1000. A match is counted together with its whole graph, so a deeper expansion means fewer matches fit — they are absent, not shortened.
brain.query.truncated.title: This answer was shortened: showing {{returned}} of {{count}} matches.
brain.query.truncated.body: What you have is the top of the ranking, in order, with nothing skipped in the middle — and every record is complete. A match is counted together with its whole graph, so a deeper expansion means fewer matches fit.
brain.query.truncated.what: To see more, raise Max response size under Show advanced, or narrow the search. A search that comes back shortened is usually a sign the question was broader than intended.
brain.query.includeFreshWrites.tooltip: Also scan the newest records directly, for when the vector index has not caught up yet. Slower, and only useful right after a write.
brain.query.includeContent.tooltip: Whether file results carry the matching passage body. Turn it off to get locations and metadata only — much smaller responses, but you will not see the text that matched.
brain.query.includeDiagnostics.tooltip: Adds the fields the system uses internally: the exact text that was embedded, the embedding model, the sync counter, and the per-stage ranking scores. Follows graph hops too, at every depth. Turn it on to work out why something ranked where it did; leave it off otherwise, because each field is returned once per result. The embedding vector itself is never returned.
brain.query.types.tooltip: Search only the checked knowledge types. Leave all unchecked to search every type.
brain.query.minPerType.tooltip: Guarantee at least this many results of this type (capped at Top K).
brain.query.filterMustBeObject: Filter must be a JSON object.

brain.query.graphShort.body: The walk hit its ceiling, so the neighbourhood shown is not all of it. The records missing are ones the walk never read — the matches themselves are unaffected.

spaces.schema.retention.hintSpace: — how long records of this type are kept; empty inherits the space default of {{days}} days

spaces.schema.retention.contentDaysHint: Removes the description, matched text and embedding, so the record stops competing in recall. Its properties, title, type and dates stay queryable.
spaces.schema.ends.label: Permitted ends
spaces.schema.ends.hint: which entity types this label may connect, and how many
spaces.schema.ends.noEntityTypes: This space declares no entity types yet, so there is nothing to pick but "no type at all". Declare them on the Entities tab first.

spaces.schema.suppressEmbeddings.label: Embeddings
spaces.schema.suppressEmbeddings.hint: Records of this type are embedded for semantic recall. Suppress it for records that are state rather than prose — rows whose text never changes but whose numbers are updated constantly.
spaces.schema.whenDuePasses.label: When the date passes
spaces.schema.whenDuePasses.hint: An entry whose date has passed normally shows as overdue. Choose “Means nothing” for a type that records something that HAPPENED — a deploy, a backup run, an alert episode — where a date in the past is the normal condition and does not mean late. Those entries keep the status you gave them.
spaces.schema.suppressEmbeddings.noBackf: Records written while this is on are not embedded, and turning it off later does not go back and embed them. Re-saving a record embeds that record.
spaces.schema.retention.contentTooLate: Detail must be dropped before the record itself is deleted at {{total}} days, otherwise it never happens.
spaces.schema.retention.libDropped: "{{name}}" was saved to the library without its retention window — a library entry cannot carry one. Set the window again on the type if you unlink it.

spaces.dangerZone.retentionDescription: Deletes records on a timer. Three tiers, most specific first: a ttlDays set on a record when it is written; then that record type's own window, set on the type in the Schema tab; then the space-wide window for that kind of record, below.
spaces.dangerZone.retentionSpaceWideHint: One window per kind of record. Each applies to records of that kind with no ttlDays of their own and no window on their type. Leave a field empty for no expiry.
brain.overview.retentionBuckets: Expiry by kind — {{list}}. Anything not listed is kept.
spaces.dangerZone.retentionPerTypeNone: No type has its own window, so the windows above are what apply.
spaces.dangerZone.retentionPerTypeHint: Edited on the type, in the Schema tab, beside its other rules. Listed here because these override the windows above:
spaces.settings.recordTtlMoved: Moved to the Danger Zone — it deletes records, so it lives with the other destructive settings.
brain.overview.retentionNone: No expiry — records are kept until deleted.
brain.overview.retentionTypeContent: {{type}}: detail dropped after {{contentDays}} d, deleted after {{days}} d
brain.overview.retentionEdit: Change in Settings → Spaces: the space-wide default in Danger Zone, a single type's window on the type in Schema
spaces.dangerZone.embeddingsDescription: Records are embedded so they can be found by meaning, not just by exact text. Suppressing that is for records that are state rather than prose — rows whose text never changes but whose numbers are updated constantly. Precedence: a single record overrides its type, and a type overrides this space-wide setting.
spaces.dangerZone.embeddingsSuppress: Do not embed records in this space
spaces.dangerZone.embeddingsNoBackfill: Records written while this is on will have no vector, and they will not appear in semantic recall. Turning it off later does not go back and embed them — use Backfill for that.
spaces.dangerZone.embeddingsPerType: These types override the setting above:
spaces.dangerZone.embeddingsBackfillBloc: Backfill is unavailable while suppression is on — every record would be skipped. Turn it off and save first.
spaces.dangerZone.embeddingsBackfillDone: Queued {{enqueued}} record(s) for embedding. This continues in the background.
spaces.dangerZone.embeddingsBackfillMore: {{remaining}} more still need embedding — run it again to continue.
spaces.dangerZone.embeddingsBackfillSkip: {{skipped}} record(s) were skipped because a type or record still suppresses them.
spaces.dangerZone.renameDescription: Changes the internal identifier used by tokens, networks, files, and MCP clients. All references updated atomically.
spaces.dangerZone.wipeDescription: Permanently deletes all brain data and files. Space configuration and ID are preserved.
spaces.dangerZone.leaveNetworksDescripti: Leaves the sync ring for each selected network.
spaces.dangerZone.deleteDescription: Permanently destroys this space along with all brain data and stored files. Cannot be undone.

spaces.dupe.intro: Configure how this space handles semantic duplicates found by the background scanner. Rules are evaluated highest-score-first; the first match decides the action.
spaces.dupe.rulesHint: When a duplicate pair scores at or above a rule threshold, its action runs. No matching rule means the pair is just flagged for review.
spaces.dupe.rulesEmpty: No rules yet. Records are just flagged for review when they look like duplicates. Add a rule to raise the bar (a higher threshold = only very close matches) or to auto-merge or notify a webhook above a score.
spaces.dupe.webhookPlaceholder: Leave empty to use webhook subscriptions
duplicates.title: Duplicate candidates
duplicates.intro: Semantically similar records found by the background scanner. Review, dismiss, or merge them.
duplicates.confirmDismiss: This removes the pair from the open list. You can still find it under "Dismissed", and a later scan may surface it again.
duplicates.empty.title: No duplicates
duplicates.empty.body: The scanner has not found any duplicate pairs in this view.
duplicates.confirmMerge: Merge these two entities? The older record is kept and the other is absorbed. This cannot be undone.
spaces.dupe.automergeWarning: Auto-merge permanently absorbs one record of each matching entity pair with no review, choosing the survivor by the Merge survivor setting above. Use a high threshold and be sure your rules are correct.
spaces.dupe.automergeConfirm: This space has an auto-merge rule. Matching entity pairs will be merged automatically and unattended, permanently absorbing one record of each pair. Save these rules?
spaces.dupe.invalidUrl: A notify rule has an invalid webhook URL.
duplicates.scanForbidden: You do not have permission to run a scan (admin only).
duplicates.reRateDone: Pair moved back to the review list.
duplicates.noMatches.title: No matches
duplicates.noMatches.body: No duplicate pairs match your search.
spaces.dupe.onInsert: Evaluate rules in real time (on insert)
spaces.dupe.onInsertHint: When on, rules also run the moment a record is inserted, not only during the scheduled scan. Applies to all inserts including bulk; leave off for scan-time only.

spaces.dangerZone.rebuildIndexesDescript: Repairs semantic search when it returns nothing. Records keep their vectors, but the search index they are queried through can be missing — after restoring a backup, or if the database search process was not ready at startup. Reindexing does not fix this; only a rebuild does. Search stays empty until the rebuild finishes.

spaces.dangerZone.rebuildIndexesStarted: Rebuilding search indexes — search results will be incomplete until it finishes.

mediaProcessing.page.title: Media Processing
mediaProcessing.page.managedBanner: These models are managed by infrastructure on this instance — settings are read-only. Change them in config.json or the environment. You can still Test connection below.
mediaProcessing.pinnedUnknown.title: {{count}} pinned field name(s) were not recognised, so they are NOT locked:
mediaProcessing.pinnedUnknown.body: These came from YTHRIL_PINNED_FIELDS. A name must be a field this page can save — check the spelling. A field the API never accepts is already fixed and needs no pin.
mediaProcessing.card.infraTitle: This value comes from the environment and cannot be changed here.
mediaProcessing.field.callBudgetHint: How long ONE request to this model may run. Empty uses the built-in default.
mediaProcessing.field.reasoningEffortHin: Check which values your model accepts — a wrong one fails every call. "none" turns thinking off and works anywhere.
mediaProcessing.verify.hint: Sends one small generated request (a 1x1 image, a moment of silence, or the word ping) to the configured model. Costs latency and, on a metered endpoint, money. A first call can take a minute while a model loads.
mediaProcessing.health.degraded: reachable, but the configured call will fail
mediaProcessing.embedding.title: Text embedding
mediaProcessing.embedding.purpose: Turns text into the vectors that power semantic search across every space.
mediaProcessing.embedding.optLocal: Local / trusted (bundled ONNX, or an internal endpoint)
mediaProcessing.embedding.endpointHint: Blank uses the bundled in-process model.
mediaProcessing.embedding.prefixQwen: Qwen — instruction on the query only
mediaProcessing.embedding.prefixSchemeHi: Asymmetric models retrieve noticeably better when the query and the stored passage are marked differently. Auto reproduces what this instance did before this setting existed — if you run nomic or Qwen behind an endpoint, set it explicitly and reindex.
mediaProcessing.embedding.reindexWarning: Changing the model, dimensions, similarity, or task prefix re-embeds every vector in every space. You will confirm on save — recall is degraded until the reindex finishes.
mediaProcessing.rerank.title: Reranker
mediaProcessing.rerank.purpose: Re-scores search candidates with a cross-encoder before they are cut to the top results.
mediaProcessing.rerank.endpointHint: Blank turns reranking off. A URL ending in /rerank is read as the text-embeddings-inference shape; anything else gets /v1/rerank appended and the Cohere/Jina shape.
mediaProcessing.rerank.multiplierHint: How many candidates the vector search fetches per requested result. A reranker can only re-order what was already found, so this over-fetch is what gives it something to rescue. 2–10, default 4.
mediaProcessing.rerank.egressWarning: This endpoint is not local. A reranker receives the search query and the passages your own data returned for it — the most revealing pairing in the system. Self-host it (for example bge-reranker-v2-m3) to keep both on this instance.
mediaProcessing.nli.title: Contradiction judge
mediaProcessing.nli.purpose: Decides whether two similar records agree or contradict. Similarity alone cannot tell them apart — two opposite claims about the same subject are usually MORE alike, not less.
mediaProcessing.nli.endpointHint: Blank leaves contradiction detection without a judge, so the Contradictions view stays empty. No sidecar ships with one — this is an encoder classifier of the roberta/deberta-MNLI family.
mediaProcessing.nli.egressWarning: This endpoint is external: pairs of record texts leave this instance to be judged. Review your data-residency policy first.
mediaProcessing.vision.title: Vision
mediaProcessing.vision.purpose: Describes uploaded images and indexes faces for search.
mediaProcessing.stt.title: Speech-to-text
mediaProcessing.stt.purpose: Transcribes uploaded audio and video so it is searchable and embeddable.
mediaProcessing.assist.title: Assist model
mediaProcessing.assist.purpose: An optional bigger, hosted model you assign to specific tasks. The only setting that sends document content off this instance.
mediaProcessing.assist.egressWarning: When assigned a task, this model receives document content — OCR-extracted text and draft transcriptions, and rendered page images for image-based tasks. That data leaves your instance.
mediaProcessing.assist.egressPending: You will confirm egress to {{host}} when you save.
mediaProcessing.render.title: Page renderer
mediaProcessing.render.purpose: Renders document pages to images for the vision model to read. It produces pictures of pages, never text — extracting text is the document converter's job.
mediaProcessing.office.title: Office renderer
mediaProcessing.office.purpose: Renders Word, Excel and PowerPoint pages to images. Separate from the page renderer because office formats need a different engine.
mediaProcessing.converter.title: Document converter
mediaProcessing.converter.purpose: Extracts text and tables from PDFs, Word documents and EPUBs. It reads a file's structure directly; it never renders pages to images, which is the page renderer's job.
mediaProcessing.docVlm.title: Document VLM
mediaProcessing.docVlm.purpose: Reads rendered document pages and transcribes them to Markdown. Runs only in the vlm, auto and max extraction modes, and only when a model is set.
mediaProcessing.docRepair.title: Document repair
mediaProcessing.docRepair.purpose: One text-only pass that reconciles a VLM transcription against the OCR text, restoring content the draft dropped. Max mode only.
mediaProcessing.docVerify.title: Document verify
mediaProcessing.docVerify.purpose: A second, independent transcription used to cross-check the first. Max mode only.
mediaProcessing.face.title: Face recognition
mediaProcessing.face.purpose: Detects faces in images and embeds them so people can be searched for.
mediaProcessing.pipelines.imagesPurpose: What happens to an uploaded image.
mediaProcessing.pipelines.audioPurpose: What happens to an uploaded audio recording.
mediaProcessing.pipelines.videoPurpose: What happens to an uploaded video: its audio is always transcribed, and at the full level each keyframe is captioned with the vision model too.
mediaProcessing.pipelines.textPurpose: What happens to the text that comes out of every other pipeline.
mediaProcessing.pipelines.configureLink: Configure this in the Models tab
mediaProcessing.pipelines.statusUnavaila: Could not read live status, so the health indicators are unknown rather than off: {{detail}}
mediaProcessing.step.caption: Caption
mediaProcessing.level.caption: Caption
mediaProcessing.tools.splitterPurpose: Separates the audio track from a video so it can be transcribed.
mediaProcessing.tools.splitterDetail: Runs in-process via ffmpeg. Nothing to configure.
mediaProcessing.tools.chunkerPurpose: Splits long text into passages, so recall can quote the passage rather than the file.
mediaProcessing.tools.chunkerDetail: Runs in-process. Whether it runs at all is the Text pipeline’s ceiling.
mediaProcessing.tools.vectorIndexPurpose: The search indexes recall depends on. Rebuild any row whose recorded state has drifted from the database.
mediaProcessing.tools.colStoredHint: What config.json records as this space's index state — checked against the live “In the database” state to surface drift.
mediaProcessing.tools.driftTitle: {{count}} space(s) claim a ready index the database does not have.
mediaProcessing.tools.driftBody: Recall in those spaces returns nothing and reports no error. Rebuild the index with the button on the row to fix it.
mediaProcessing.tools.indexEmpty: No spaces with their own indexes.
mediaProcessing.modeDesc.off: Documents are stored but never read. No text is extracted, so nothing from them can be recalled.
mediaProcessing.modeDesc.ocr: The OCR sidecar (Tesseract) reads text and tables from each page. Fast, fully local, no vision model needed.
mediaProcessing.modeDesc.vlm: Render each page and transcribe it with the vision model, grounded on the OCR text.
mediaProcessing.modeDesc.repair: VLM, plus a repair pass that reconciles the draft against the OCR text — and a second-model consensus pass when a verify model is set.
mediaProcessing.modeDesc.auto: As much as this instance can do: the repair pass when a repair model is configured, otherwise the vision model, otherwise OCR.
mediaProcessing.docSummary.off: Not read at all — documents are stored but never analysed
mediaProcessing.docSummary.fallback: Mode is {{mode}}, but no vision model — falls back to OCR
mediaProcessing.docSummary.repaired: Read by {{mode}} — OCR-grounded {{model}} vision, repaired against OCR
mediaProcessing.confirm.egressTitle: Send document content to an external model?
mediaProcessing.confirm.egressMessage: The model at {{host}} will receive document content — OCR-extracted text and draft transcriptions, and rendered page images for image-based tasks. This data leaves your instance and is subject to that provider’s handling. Enable egress to {{host}}?
mediaProcessing.confirm.reindexTitle: Change the embedding model — re-index everything?
mediaProcessing.confirm.reindexMessage: Changing the embedding model, dimensions, or similarity means every stored vector in every space must be RE-EMBEDDED. Recall is degraded until it finishes, and on a large instance this can take a long while. Only continue if you understand what you are doing.
mediaProcessing.confirm.discardMessage: You have unsaved changes on this tab. Switching tabs discards them.
mediaProcessing.pipelines.ceilingHint: Each pipeline below carries an instance ceiling — the most any space may do with that class. A space can choose less, never more: lowering a ceiling caps every space already above it, and those spaces keep their own choice if you raise it again.
mediaProcessing.pipelines.ceilingOffWarn: Off applies everywhere — no space can process this class.
mediaProcessing.pipelines.firstStepDown: The first step of this pipeline is unavailable, so only Off and Auto can be selected. Configure it on the Models tab.
files.progress.stalled: No progress reported — this job may be stuck
mediaProcessing.face.confidenceHint: Similarity (0–1) above which a face is labelled automatically. Below it the face is embedded but left unlabelled.
mediaProcessing.confirm.faceEgressMessag: Face images detected in your files will be sent to {{host}} for recognition. Face data is biometric data. Only continue if you control that endpoint or accept its data handling.
mediaProcessing.confirm.faceEgressTitle: Send face crops to an external service?
mediaProcessing.face.egressPending: Not yet acknowledged: saving will ask you to confirm that face crops may be sent to {{host}}.
mediaProcessing.face.apiKeyPlaceholder: Leave blank to keep the stored key
mediaProcessing.face.endpointHint: Leave empty to run face detection in-process. A configured endpoint receives face crops — biometric data — and must be acknowledged before it is used. If it is unreachable, processing falls back to in-process.
mediaProcessing.face.minSizeHint: As a fraction of the image’s shorter side. Smaller faces are skipped, which avoids noise from crowd shots.
mediaProcessing.face.personTypesHint: Chosen from your Schema Library entity types. Only entities of these types can enter the face gallery, so linking a location or object to a photo can never poison it.
mediaProcessing.face.personTypesEmpty: No entity types in your Schema Library yet — define some there to select them here.
spaces.schema.propertySchemasHint: — the properties this type declares; how strictly they are enforced follows the validation setting above
mediaProcessing.face.gatedByPipeline: Face recognition follows the Images pipeline: raise it to "Caption + face recognition" to detect and embed faces. Requires the local model files to be present.
mediaProcessing.face.enabledPinned: Your infrastructure has pinned whether face recognition may run at all (FACE_RECOGNITION_ENABLED). The endpoint below, and your acknowledgement of it, are still yours to set — they are a different decision.
mediaProcessing.face.awaitingAck: This endpoint is saved but NOT in use: egress to {{host}} has not been acknowledged, so faces are handled by the built-in model instead. Save this card, or raise the Images pipeline to face recognition, to be asked.
mediaProcessing.assist.gatedByPipeline: Used for the document repair pass. Raise Document extraction to "Repair" (or Auto) to route repairs through it; you will be asked to acknowledge the egress.

review.title: Review
review.suggestions.intro: What this space declared it would hold, measured against what it actually holds. Every point lost names a specific missing thing.
review.suggestions.loadError: The completeness checks could not be loaded. This is not the same as a space with nothing to fix.
review.suggestions.clean.title: Nothing to suggest
review.suggestions.clean.body: Every check this space can be measured against already passes.
review.suggestions.none.title: Nothing to measure yet
review.suggestions.none.body: This space declares no schemas and holds no records, so there is nothing to check it against. Add a purpose, some type schemas, or content.
review.suggestions.why.declared-type-unu: The schema promises a vocabulary the space never used — usually a typo, or a model that was planned and abandoned.
review.suggestions.why.undeclared-type-i: These are exactly the records strict validation would now reject. The debt is already taken on; turning validation up will surface it.
review.suggestions.why.declared-property: A declared field that nothing fills is a field nobody knew to fill. Either start filling it or drop it from the schema.
review.suggestions.why.entity-without-ed: An entity graph with no edges is a list. These records can be found by search, but nothing can be reached through them.
review.suggestions.why.file-not-recallab: Recall cannot reach these in any form — not as a whole file, not as a chunk. Uploading them accomplished nothing yet.
review.suggestions.why.meta-purpose-miss: MCP clients read the purpose at handshake. Without one, every connecting agent starts with no idea what this space is for.
review.suggestions.why.schemas-declared-: The space wrote rules and turned off the referee. Set validation to warn or strict in the space's Schema settings.
review.contradictions.intro: Records in this space that disagree with each other — same subject, opposite claims.
review.contradictions.noneWithStatusBody: No contradiction has that status yet. Switch back to Open to see what still needs review.
review.contradictions.structuredOnlyBody: The deterministic pass ran and found no record setting the same single-valued property to two different values. Configure an NLI (entailment) model under Settings → Media Processing to also catch records that disagree in prose.
review.contradictions.cleanBody: No contradictions were found in this space.
review.contradictions.judgeRan: Both passes have run here — the deterministic field check and the entailment judge.
review.contradictions.scanStalled: The scan finished, but the entailment judge was unreachable, so model-judged pairs were not settled. It will resume where it stopped.
review.contradictions.decidedBy: Decided by {{who}}. Nothing was deleted — the superseded record is kept and marked.
review.contradictions.noEdge: Decision recorded. No edge was drawn: edges connect entities, and this pair is not one.
review.contradictions.fullError: This record could not be loaded — do not decide from the summary alone.
review.typeFilter.label: Record type
review.typeFilter.capped: Showing the first 500 findings — filters apply to those only.
review.typeFilter.noneOfTypeBody: There are findings in this queue, but none of the selected record type. Choose All types to see them.

brain.overview.er.hint: Inferred from this space's schema and from the records actually stored.
brain.overview.er.diagramLabel: Entity relationship diagram for this space
brain.overview.er.empty: No entity types yet — this space has no entities and declares no types.
brain.overview.er.loadFailed: Could not load the data model
brain.overview.er.truncated: This space is larger than one read: the {{scan}} scan stopped at {{limit}} records, so the diagram is partial.
brain.overview.er.dangling: {{n}} edges point at an entity that no longer exists.
brain.overview.er.proxy: A proxy space has no single data model — open a member space to see one.
tokens.matrix.help: Set a level per area per space. Replaces the permission and space choices above — a token uses one or the other, never both.
tokens.rights.title: Rights
tokens.rights.instanceLevelHint: Not a rung on a space — these apply to the whole instance. A space-restricted administrator cannot grant them.
tokens.rights.spaceAdmin.desc: Administers one space: all four areas at admin. Grants that space’s own tokens and settings. It is derived — it means exactly the four cells to its left set to A, and it is a shortcut for setting them together.
tokens.rights.spaceAdmin.on: Administer this space (sets all four areas to admin)
tokens.rights.spaceAdmin.off: Not an administrator of this space (clears all four areas)
tokens.rights.notAreaScoped: Space-scoped routes that no area governs, and why:
tokens.own.title: Your access
tokens.own.readOnly: What the token you are signed in with may do. Read-only — changing it needs an administrator.
tokens.own.legacy: This token predates the rights model and carries no grid. It works exactly as before; an administrator can convert it.
tokens.listNeedsAdmin: Listing every token on the instance needs administrator rights. Your own access is shown above.
spaces.schema.propDetail.mergeFnUnavaila: — no merge function applies to this type
tokens.rights.endpointsUnavailable: The endpoint list could not be loaded. The descriptions above still apply.
tokens.rights.clamp.floor: Held at {{rung}} by the all-spaces floor
tokens.rights.clamp.implied: Held at {{rung}} because {{area}} is {{cause}}, which cannot work without it
tokens.rights.area.knowledge.desc: Memories, entities, relationships and timeline entries — the records the space is made of, and searching them.
tokens.rights.area.files.desc: Documents stored in the space: reading them, writing them, and the folder structure they live in.
tokens.rights.area.schema.desc: The shape the space expects its records to take — which types exist and which properties they carry.
tokens.rights.area.dataQuality.desc: Finding and resolving duplicates, contradictions and gaps, and the review decisions that follow.
tokens.rights.rung.read.desc: may look at everything in this area and change nothing — an agent can search and read, and every write it tries is refused
tokens.rights.rung.write.desc: everything read allows, plus creating, editing and deleting individual records — this is the level normal MCP use needs
tokens.rights.rung.admin.desc: everything write allows, plus the settings and the irreversible operations for this area, such as emptying a collection
brain.tab.spaceSettingsTitle: Configure this space — label, schema, duplicates, danger zone
tokens.mfa.codeHint: Granting an exemption needs a current code from your authenticator, even if this token is exempt itself.
tokens.danger.title: Danger zone
tokens.danger.rotateHint: Generates a new secret and stops the old one working immediately. The new value is shown once.
tokens.danger.revokeHint: Deletes this token. It can never be used again.
brain.overview.useResetHint: Clear this space’s recorded usage. Irreversible.
brain.overview.confirmUsageReset: This deletes the recorded usage history for {{label}}. The panel will read zero and start counting again. This cannot be undone.
tokens.rights.plain.knowledge.none: Your agent cannot see this space at all.
tokens.rights.plain.knowledge.read: Your agent can search and read records, and change nothing.
tokens.rights.plain.knowledge.write: Your agent can add, edit and delete single records — what normal MCP use needs.
tokens.rights.plain.knowledge.admin: Your agent can also empty whole collections, and rebuild or re-embed the space’s search index — none of which can be undone.
tokens.rights.plain.files.none: Your agent cannot see this space's files.
tokens.rights.plain.files.read: Your agent can list and read files, and add nothing.
tokens.rights.plain.files.write: Your agent can upload, edit, move and delete files — what normal MCP use needs.
tokens.rights.plain.files.admin: Your agent can also delete file records wholesale.
tokens.rights.plain.schema.none: Your agent cannot see how this space is structured.
tokens.rights.plain.schema.read: Your agent can see which record types exist and which fields they expect.
tokens.rights.plain.schema.write: Your agent can change the space's types and rules, which affects every later write.
tokens.rights.plain.schema.admin: Your agent can also replace the whole type map in one call, which is the only way to delete a type.
tokens.rights.plain.dataQuality.none: Your agent cannot see duplicate or contradiction reviews.
tokens.rights.plain.dataQuality.read: Your agent can see flagged duplicates and contradictions, and resolve none.
tokens.rights.plain.dataQuality.write: Your agent can resolve, merge and dismiss what review flags, and start a scan itself.
tokens.rights.plain.dataQuality.admin: Your agent can also switch on merging as records are written, so duplicates are combined without anyone looking.
embedding.origins.title: Origins allowed to embed this instance
embedding.origins.subtitle: A portal listed here may show Ythril inside its own page. Nothing is allowed by default.
embedding.origins.warning: Listing an origin grants two things together: permission to display Ythril inside a frame, and permission to restyle it at runtime. Both can be used to impersonate this interface, so add only origins you operate or trust to the same degree.
embedding.origins.none: No origin is listed. Ythril can only be framed by itself.
embedding.origins.hint: One exact origin per line: scheme, host and port only, with no path. https is required except on localhost. Wildcards are never accepted. A change takes effect on the next request.
tokens.create.rateLimitHint: Leave blank to use the instance default. Set a lower number for a client doing bulk work, so it cannot crowd out everything else.
tokens.filter.spacesSortHint: Sorts by reach: schema library, then fewest spaces, then all spaces
tokens.empty.filteredBody: Your tokens are still there — the search boxes are hiding them.
graph.recordUnavailable.file: This file has no record view here — open it from the Files tab.
graph.recordUnavailable.derived: This connection is derived from a link, not a stored relationship, so it has no record of its own.
networks.network.invite.secretWarning: Send this the way you would send a password. Anyone who has it can complete the join. It expires after 24 hours and can only be used once.
networks.dialog.join.error.invalidCode: That does not look like an invite code. Copy the whole line the other brain produced — it starts with ythril1_.
